numbers.text: Methods: Fifty individuals with moderate-to-severe AUD were randomized to receive semaglutide (3 mg/day for 4 weeks, then 7 mg/day for 4 weeks) or placebo for 8 weeks.

Participants were randomized to receive semaglutide (3 mg/day for four weeks, then 7 mg/day for four weeks) or placebo for eight weeks in an approximate 1:1 ratio using an urn randomization procedure(32) that balanced sex and BMI (≥30 vs. <30 kg/m2) between treatment groups.
This phase 2, double-blind, randomized, parallel-arm trial evaluated the effects of oral semaglutide on alcohol craving and consumption among treatment-seeking adults with Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD).
Key preregistered secondary outcomes were heavy drinking days (HDD) and drinks per day (DPD) during the last four weeks of treatment.
The primary outcome was laboratory-based alcohol cue-elicited craving at Week 6.
Significantly more semaglutide than placebo participants reduced their risk drinking level by one or more levels (Wald χ2(1)=4.01, p=0.045).
